# Localization

The texts of the library itself (button labels, empty states, screen reader texts) in English and Simplified Chinese, and how to replace them.

## builtinMessages

The complete text tables of the built-in languages, by language name: `builtinMessages['zh-CN']` is `zhCN`. To
translate the library into another language, start from one of them and pass your table to ThemeProvider's
`locale`.

```ts
const builtinMessages: Readonly<Record<LocaleName, Readonly<Record<MessageKey, string>>>>
```

## formatMessage

Looks up a built-in text and fills in its placeholders. `messages` is the text table to look in: a key missing
from it falls back to the English text, and a key missing from both returns the key itself. `params` fills the
`{name}` placeholders, such as `{ name: 'Report' }` for `Type "{name}" to confirm`; a placeholder without a value
stays as it is. Returns the text. Components use it through useT; call it directly outside React.

```ts
formatMessage(messages: Messages, key: MessageKey, params?: Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>): string
```

## useT

Hook that returns the translation function of the current language, `t(key, params)`: it looks up a built-in
text in the text table of the nearest ThemeProvider or LocaleProvider (English outside them) and fills in
`{name}` placeholders like formatMessage. The function changes only when the language changes. Use it in your
own components to show texts of the library, such as `t('error.retry')`.

```ts
useT(): (key: "theme.default" | "colorMode.light" | "colorMode.dark" | "colorMode.system" | "empty.description" | "spin.loading" | "error.title" | "error.retry" | "confirm.ok" | "confirm.cancel" | ... 170 more ... | "dataTable.columns.reset", params?: Readonly<...> | undefined) => string
```

## zhCN

The built-in Simplified Chinese texts: a frozen text table with the same keys as `enUS`. Select it with
`locale="zh-CN"` on ThemeProvider.

```ts
const zhCN: Readonly<Record<keyof typeof enUS, string>>
```

## LocaleProvider

Switches the language of part of the page: the built-in texts of the components inside it and the locale of
the wrapped Ant Design components. Theme, color mode and density stay those of the surrounding
ThemeProvider, and the global locale of dayjs is not changed (the date pickers inside still follow `locale`).
Use it to preview components in a language other than the application's, for example in documentation;
the language of the application itself is set on ThemeProvider.

```ts
<LocaleProvider {...props} />
```

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `LocaleName \| Messages` | Language: the built-in `en-US` or `zh-CN`, or the text table of a custom language (missing keys fall back to en-US). | `'en-US'` | No |
| `messages` | `Messages` | Overrides or adds individual texts on top of `locale`. | — | No |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content shown in this language. | — | No |

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### LocaleName

A built-in language: `en-US` (English, the default) or `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese).

```ts
type LocaleName = 'en-US' | 'zh-CN'
```

### Messages

A text table: key → text. Texts may contain `{name}` placeholders, which formatMessage fills in. Used for the
`locale` and `messages` of ThemeProvider and LocaleProvider; the keys are the built-in `MessageKey`s, and other keys
(such as the `nameKey` of a custom theme) are allowed too.

```ts
type Messages = Readonly<Partial<Record<MessageKey, string>>> &
  Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```
